evidence.field: 形義通解；字形分類；出土用例
evidence.text: The database describes 會 in oracle-bone and bronze forms as 合 plus a container-like element: a lid covering a vessel and its contents, with the proposed original sense ‘fit together’. It reports oracle-bone 《合集》1030正「會我」 as a damaged, uncertain possible ‘meet/assemble’ use; bronze inscription 𠫑羌鐘「入長城，先會于平陰」 uses it for meeting at a place. The database also reports a bronze form with 彳 in some inscriptions and interprets it as meeting on a road. Warring States bamboo texts use 會 for joining, e.g. 郭店《語叢一》36 「所以會天道人道也」. These are separate records of graphic analysis and lexical uses; the oracle-bone ‘meeting’ reading is explicitly tentative.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.text: The article says oracle-bone forms grouped as 會 include three types: one from 合 plus 皿, and two from 合 plus a 日-like or frame-like middle element. It treats the 日/frame shapes as likely one graphic type, while reviewing differing earlier cataloguing decisions. The available search result gave the article’s own text, but opening the PDF returned an access/internal error, so its detailed argument and later sections were not inspected.
evidence.title: 吳品婕：《「合」與「會」甲骨金文用法重探》

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 異體字 A01840-001; 會 variant entry
evidence.text: The dictionary identifies 会 as a variant of 會 and says the 会 shape arose in cursive writing, was used widely in later common regular-script writing, and was adopted in the PRC simplified-character list. Thus 会 is historically a graphic simplification/variant of 會, not an ancient 人+云 construction. The same entry records variant pronunciations guì, kuài, huǐ and huì for 會.
evidence.title: [A01840] 會 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The page quotes Xu Shen’s 《說文》: 「會，合也。从亼从曾省。曾，益也。」 This is a historical lexicographic analysis: ‘combine/meet’, from 亼 and an abbreviated 曾, with 曾 explained as ‘increase’. The modern paleographic account on the same page instead analyzes early forms through 合 and a vessel/lid image. These are distinguishable accounts and the 《說文》 component explanation does not by itself confirm the vessel interpretation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.field: 《廣韻》 readings and Middle Chinese categories
evidence.text: The page records 會 fanqie 黃外 and 古外, both 去聲, 蟹攝泰韻合一; the initials are 匣 (voiced guttural) and 見 (voiceless velar), corresponding to distinct readings. Its table lists modern Mandarin huì and kuài. The repository Baxter–Sagart TSV, checked locally, has exact rows for 會: huì / Middle Chinese hwajH / Old Chinese *m-kˤop-s for ‘meeting; have a meeting’; another huì form *ɦʷˤajs is an Eastern Han transcription gloss; and kuài / kwajH / *kˤop-s for ‘calculate; calculation’. These repository spellings have been preserved exactly and kept sense-distinct. No claim is made that either reading represents the pronunciation of a putative component in 会.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.source: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction appendix (secondary rendering of dataset)
evidence.text: The inspected table gives the meeting reading as Middle Chinese hwajH and Old Chinese *m-kˁop-s, gloss ‘come together’, and warns that this appendix is outdated relative to Baxter and Sagart’s 2014 book. The local structured TSV independently checked for this task uses *m-kˤop-s and *kˤop-s for its separate rows. The differing notation is reported rather than silently reconciled; the local TSV notation governs the local-data report.
evidence.title: Appendix:Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction

evidence.source: 字通 via Kotobank / 日本国語大辞典
evidence.field: 會 character account and Japanese lexical attestation
evidence.text: 字通 presents the traditional character 会 as 會 and analyzes its older form as a covered cooking vessel, with a lower steamer and upper lidded vessel; it interprets the lid’s fitting as a semantic bridge to ‘fit/meet’. It says the meeting sense appears in oracle-bone/bronze forms and, more specifically, that use of 會 for ‘meeting’ is visible in the Warring States/early regional-state period and Qin and Xu bronzes. This is a source’s account, not independently settled proof of the vessel identification. Separately, the Japanese kun reading/word え ‘gathering, especially a religious assembly’ is dated in 日本霊異記 (810–824), with an example 「会を設けて供養しき」; this records a Japanese lexical use, not the origin of the graph.
evidence.title: 会(カイ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.field: Bronze and Warring States lexical attestations
evidence.text: For graphic development versus word history, the page reports a possible oracle-bone meeting use in 《合集》1030正, a bronze meeting use in 𠫑羌鐘 「入長城，先會于平陰」, and Warring States bamboo examples for bringing things/ideas together and treaty meeting. It also reports another bronze use for an account/record book in 訓匜. These distinct senses should not be treated as a chronology inferred from modern dictionary gloss order; the inscriptions provide separate attestation contexts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.field: Detailed explanation; citations and noun senses
evidence.text: The dictionary cites early received-text senses for ‘assemble/meet’ including 《詩·小雅·車攻》「會同有絳」 and 《詩·唐風·杕杜》「會言近止」, and later historical narrative examples including 《史記·廉頗藺相如列傳》 meeting at the border and 《史記·陳涉世家》 accounting/calculation usage. It separately lists the noun ‘lid/cover’, citing 《儀禮·士喪禮》 and 《儀禮·士虞禮》 for opening the 會. These establish attested lexical senses in cited texts but do not establish which sense chronologically preceded the other without dating and textual-history analysis.
evidence.title: 會 huì、kuài、kuò - 汉典

evidence.text: The dictionary’s component connections for 會 are 合, 口, 𠓛 (container lid), and 彳 in certain bronze variants. It does not identify 人 or 云 as ancient components of 會, and its reading table concerns 會 itself. The local Baxter–Sagart dataset has no row for 云 in this query and no independent component reading data establishing 云 as the phonetic of 会. Therefore the dossier’s 人+云 mnemonic/analysis is unsupported as a historical account; the graph 会 is a later cursive-derived form of 會.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.text: This Hong Kong educational resource explains early 會 as the lower part of a 甗 steamer, its perforated partition in the middle, and a lid above; it says the graph depicts cooking vessels being fitted together. This is a specific vessel-identification proposal and conflicts in detail with CUHK’s more general vessel/lid/container interpretation and with Xu Shen’s component analysis. The page lists forms for oracle, bronze, seal, and standard scripts, but their images were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 會

evidence.text: The government character database records 會 U+6703 and gives Mandarin readings guì, kuài, huǐ, huì; it also records Taiwan Hakka and Taiwanese readings including ē, hē, huē, kuè. These are modern pronunciation records, not evidence of the ancient shapes or of a phonetic component in simplified 会.
evidence.title: 字形資訊 - [會] 1-6444 - 全字庫 CNS11643 (2024)

search_audit.outcome: Search performed. CUHK was inspected for fanqie and categories. Chinese Text Project and Guangyun page opens returned internal errors; search-result metadata was not treated as inspected page evidence. No independently verified phonological basis for a Min Nan ē borrowing/cognacy proposal was located.

gaps: The Academia Sinica evolution page exposed only a skeletal page listing script stages; no glyph images were visually inspected. The NCCU paper’s PDF open failed, so only its search-result passage was usable; its full argument remains unreviewed.

The early graph’s central shape is interpreted differently across sources: a generic vessel/lid with contents, a cooking vessel/甗 assembly, and Xu Shen’s 亼 plus abbreviated 曾. The exact depicted object and whether the graph originally depicted a food steamer remain disputed or insufficiently demonstrated by the inspected material.

The oracle-bone 《合集》1030正 «會我» interpretation is explicitly tentative and the text is fragmentary. A secure earliest dated semantic use of ‘meet/gather’ versus a separate lid/container use was not established. The claimed ‘meeting’ bronze attestation is a secondary database report; inscription plates were not inspected.

The sources do not demonstrate a sound component in 會 or a historical phonetic role for 云 in 会. No independent pronunciation evidence for 云 was used, and 会’s derivation from cursive 會 makes a 人+云 origin implausible as graphic history.

Possible semantic extension from fitting a lid to joining/meeting is an interpretation, not a fully documented chronology. The dated record supports separate container/lid and meeting senses, but does not establish the path or direction of semantic development.

Modern Mandarin huì and kuài, Cantonese wui6 (from dossier), and Taiwanese ē forms represent distinct reading traditions/senses. The proposed Min Nan ē derivation from 解 was not independently verified from a primary dialectological source; a secondary search result mentioned it, but its supporting work was not inspected.

The outdated secondary Baxter–Sagart appendix prints *m-kˁop-s; the local structured dataset prints *m-kˤop-s. These notation differences are preserved. The KUài ‘calculate’ reading has its own *kˤop-s row and should not be conflated with the meeting reading.
